role: Mordell–Weil ranks of genus-1 fibres of the ES surface at hard primes
missing_theorem: For every large p, some genus-1 fibre E_{p,s} of an elliptic fibration of U_p has positive rank and a positive integral point that is an ES solution. The plane-section fibration has generic Mordell–Weil rank 0 (Shioda–Tate), and by the scaling isomorphism U_p ≅ U_1 over ℚ, fibre ranks do not depend on p. Integrality is the only p-dependent condition.
status_ref: BRAINSTORM/elliptic_fibration_es.md §2 (Shioda–Tate: MW rank 8 − (1+2+0+5) = 0); GEOMETRY_ES §1: over ℚ (indeed over ℤ[1/n]) x = nX identifies U_n ≅ U_1, so every geometric/Galois invariant is independent of n; n enters only through the integral model (ES(n) ⟺ U_1 has a positive rational point with denominators dividing n)
barrier: B2 (integrality = divisor condition); rank is n-independent
note: Hard vs easy primes cannot differ in any rational-geometry invariant of U_p.

role: calibration: the cheapest-certificate height anticorrelates with class-number data
missing_theorem: None for ES beyond calibration. PROVED here: every (★) solution (uBC, pBC, puC) has max denominator p·C·max(u, B) ≤ p·uBC ≤ p(p+1)/3 (since u + B ≤ uBC + 1 gives 3uBC ≤ p + 1). So minz(p) > p(p+1)/3 forces R(p) = 0, and large minz is a (★)-failure detector, whose frequency depends on L-values through M_BM.
status_ref: this pass, scripts/z52d_avenue_Q09_primitive_height.py (2) (no prime < 2600 with minz > p(p+1)/3 and R > 0); data/z52b/classical_corr.json (−0.136 unnormalised); BM_LVALUE Thm A
next: Optional: regress log(minz/p) on log L(1, χ_p) and log L(1, χ_{−4p}) together (Pass 1 did one variable).
note: Calibration; the height–hardness link is the elementary bound above.

role: height-bounded ES: every prime has a solution with max denominator ≤ p² (or ≤ c·p²)
missing_theorem: For every prime p a solution with max(x, y, z) ≤ c·p². PROVED here: any (★) solution has max ≤ p(p+1)/3, so the statement with c = 1/3 + o(1) follows from R(p) ≥ 1, and the only primes needing larger height are (★)-failures. Lower bound: every solution has max ≥ p^{3/2}/2 (out_Q03 Z0644). So height-bounded ES at exponent 2 is (★)/Type II-strength, and at exponent < 3/2 it is false.
status_ref: this pass (bound above; script (2)); Pass 1 U04 (z ≤ p² never fails ≤ 10⁵; z ≤ p^{1.75} fails at 50 primes); out_Q03 Z0644
next: None. Record the bound minz ≤ p(p+1)/3 whenever R(p) ≥ 1 next to the variants data.
note: The exponent-2 'limit' is explained: (★) solutions live below p²/3.

role: primitive ES (gcd(x, y, z) = 1) as a sharper sibling of (★)
missing_theorem: PROVED here (elementary): for primes p ≡ 1 (4), Type I solutions are never primitive, and every Type II solution is (abk, pkma, pkmb) with gcd(a, b) = 1, m | a + b, p = 4abk − (a+b)/m, gcd(x, y, z) = k. So the primitive solutions are exactly k = 1: p = 4ab − (a+b)/m. (★) is the dual line m = 1 (k = C). (a, m) = (1, 1) gives p = 3b − 1, so every p ≡ 2 (mod 3) has a primitive solution; this explains 'all failures ≡ 1 (mod 12)'. Missing theorem: every large prime p ≡ 1 (12) has coprime a, b and m | a + b with p = 4ab − (a+b)/m.
status_ref: this pass, scripts/z52d_avenue_Q09_primitive_height.py (1): all 798 primitive solutions for primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 2600 have this form; failures 13, 37, …, 2557 are all ≡ 1 (12). They contain all 15 failures < 2600 of the d = 1 shot family (COMPOSITION_ES / GROWING_MUTE: 13, 37, 97, …; 99 primes < 10⁶) plus 277, 373, 853, 2221, 2557 (script (3)). Pass 1 U04: 110 failures ≤ 10⁵, 56 of them ≤ 2·10⁴ (density thinning).
barrier: B2 (single-integer lottery with a smaller mean); B2 Thm 2.2(iii) does not apply (infinitely many slices)
next: Extend the primitive-failure census to 10⁷ with the (a, b, m) form (a sieve over m | a + b is cheap) and fit the decay. If the failures thin like (★)'s, primitive ES is a cleaner ES-strength target with the explicit dual structure k ↔ m.
note: Cleanest new structural fact of the batch: (★) and primitive ES are the two coordinate lines k = C, m = 1 and k = 1 of one Type II parameter plane.
